data.gender_notes: Anuendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anuendra is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Anu', meaning 'Anu' or 'Lord of'. The name 'Endra' comes from the word 'Indra', the king of gods in Hindu mythology. Anuendra is thus a name that signifies power, strength, and divine protection. The name Anuendra carries the meaning “Lord of Anu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anuendra usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of anu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name blessed by gods, inspiring courage and wisdom.

data.cultural_impact: Anuendra carries a rich cultural heritage as it contains the name of the Hindu deity, Indra. Indra, the god of rain, thunderbolts, and war, is one of the most ancient and revered deities in Hinduism. Anuendra evokes images of power, strength, and divine blessings associated with Indra.
data.spiritual_significance: Anuendra is a name that resonates with the profound spiritual significance of invoking the blessings of the supreme deity Indra. historical_references.reference: Anuendra was a king of the Anušeyin Dynasty who ruled from 1206 to 1242 AD in the region of present-day Bangladesh.
Anuendra is also mentioned in the Puranic literature as the name of a king of the lunar dynasty who ruled over Hastinapura during the Mahabharata era.

On Reddit, there is a growing community of Indian mythology enthusiasts who discuss and share their knowledge of Hindu gods and legends, including 'Anuendra'. On Goodreads, several fantasy literature books feature 'Anuendra' as a character or element in their stories. Lastly, on Tabletop Simulator, a popular virtual tabletop game platform, there are role-playing games based on Indian mythology where players can assume the role of 'Anuendra' or interact with him in the game world.
